claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used to produce a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The proposed transition arises from the unique properties of compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys.
The material initial state is a conventional alloy.
Temper embrittlement is the intervention applied to the material.
Temper embrittlement occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Temper embrittlement produces a loss of ductility.
Temper embrittlement is ubiquitous in conventional alloys.
Temper embrittlement has not been reported in compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems.
The predicted outcome is a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The exact mechanism of temper embrittlement is not fully understood.
Ductility of compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys can be tested across a narrow temperature window.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes a ductile–brittle–ductile transition in compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys to temper-embrittlement-related behavior, while the mechanism field states that temper embrittlement has not been reported in those alloy systems.

The initial material and baseline are identified as conventional alloys, whereas the hypothesis and proposed experiment target compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys; the intended material system is therefore inconsistent.
